_about: Public-domain Pasquier Quesnel (1634-1719), the Oratorian whose Moral Reflections were condemned in the bull Unigenitus, in English translation for the Word Hoard: The New Testament with Moral Reflections upon every Verse (London, 1719-1725, four volumes, dedications signed by Richard Russel) and The Gospels with Moral Reflections on each Verse, with Daniel Wilson's introductory essay (Glasgow: Collins, 1830, three volumes), from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-18 by lane A, round 35 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

quesnel-nt-reflections-1: The New Testament, with Moral Reflections upon every Verse, vol. I (London: J. R. for R. Bonwicke, T. Goodwin and others, 1719; catalogued 1725 in error)
quesnel-nt-reflections-2: The New Testament, with Moral Reflections upon every Verse, written in French by Father Quesnel and now translated into English, vol. II, part 1 (London: R. H. for R. Bonwicke and others; year not read)
quesnel-nt-reflections-3: The New Testament, with Moral Reflections upon every Verse, vol. III (London: R. and J. Bonwicke, R. Wilkin and J. Walthoe, 1725)
quesnel-nt-reflections-4: The New Testament, with Moral Reflections upon every Verse, vol. IV, part II (London: R. and J. Bonwicke, R. Wilkin, J. Walthoe and T. Ward, 1725)
quesnel-gospels-1: The Gospels, with Moral Reflections on each Verse, with an introductory essay by Daniel Wilson, vol. I (Glasgow: William Collins, 1830)
quesnel-gospels-2: The Gospels, with Moral Reflections on each Verse, vol. II (Glasgow: William Collins, 1830)
quesnel-gospels-3: The Gospels, with Moral Reflections on each Verse, vol. III (Glasgow: William Collins, 1830)
